column4: description

column3: HS-LS1-1: Structure of DNA determines structure of proteins
column4: Construct an explanation based on evidence for how the structure of DNA determines the structure of proteins which carry out the essential functions of life through systems of specialized cells.
I can describe how a DNA sequence is copied (transcribed) and read (translated) to build a protein.
I can explain how the order of amino acids determines a protein's shape and function.
I can use evidence to explain how proteins carry out functions in specialized cells.

column3: HS-LS1-2: Interacting systems in multicellular organisms
column4: Develop and use a model to illustrate the hierarchical organization of interacting systems that provide specific functions within multicellular organisms.
I can order levels of organization from cells to tissues, organs, organ systems, and organisms.
I can model how two or more body systems work together to perform a function.
I can explain how a problem in one system affects other systems.
Plan and conduct an investigation to provide evidence that feedback mechanisms maintain homeostasis.
I can explain negative and positive feedback and give examples of each.
I can plan an investigation with a testable question, variables, and a procedure.
I can use data to show how a feedback mechanism keeps conditions stable.
Use a model to illustrate the role of cellular division (mitosis) and differentiation in producing and maintaining complex organisms.
I can model the stages of the cell cycle and mitosis.
I can explain how mitosis produces genetically identical cells for growth and repair.
I can explain how differentiation produces specialized cells from the same DNA.
Use a model to illustrate how photosynthesis transforms light energy into stored chemical energy.
I can identify the reactants and products of photosynthesis.
I can model how light energy becomes chemical energy stored in glucose.
I can explain where photosynthesis happens in a cell and why it matters.

column3: HS-LS1-6: From sugar to amino acids and large molecules
column4: Construct and revise an explanation based on evidence for how carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen from sugar molecules may combine with other elements to form amino acids and/or other large carbon-based molecules.
I can name the elements in sugar, amino acids, and proteins, and say which elements must come from somewhere other than sugar.
I can use atom accounting to show that atoms are rearranged, not created or destroyed, when molecules are built.
I can explain how monomers (amino acids) bond to form polymers (proteins) and other large molecules.
I can construct an explanation (claim, evidence, reasoning) using data about how sugar and other elements form building blocks.
I can revise an explanation using new evidence or feedback.

Use a model to illustrate that cellular respiration is a chemical process whereby the bonds of food molecules and oxygen molecules are broken and the bonds in new compounds are formed, resulting in a net transfer of energy.
I can identify the reactants and products of cellular respiration.
I can model how bonds are broken and formed to transfer energy.
I can compare photosynthesis and cellular respiration.
Use mathematical and/or computational representations to support explanations of factors that affect carrying capacity of ecosystems at different scales.
I can identify limiting factors and define carrying capacity.
I can read and graph population data.
I can use data to explain how changes in factors affect carrying capacity.
Use mathematical representations to support and revise explanations based on evidence about factors affecting biodiversity and populations in ecosystems of different scales.
I can calculate and compare measures of biodiversity and population size.
I can explain how factors such as competition and predation affect populations.
I can revise an explanation when new population data is presented.

column3: HS-LS2-3: Matter and energy with and without oxygen
column4: Construct and revise an explanation based on evidence for the cycling of matter and flow of energy in aerobic and anaerobic conditions.
I can compare aerobic respiration and fermentation.
I can explain how matter cycles and energy flows under each condition.
I can revise an explanation using new evidence.
Use mathematical representations to support claims for the cycling of matter and flow of energy among organisms in an ecosystem.
I can trace energy through food chains, food webs, and energy pyramids.
I can calculate the energy available at each trophic level.
I can explain why energy decreases at each level while matter cycles.

column3: HS-LS2-5: Photosynthesis and respiration in the carbon cycle
column4: Develop a model to illustrate the role of photosynthesis and cellular respiration in the cycling of carbon among the biosphere, atmosphere, hydrosphere, and geosphere.
I can identify carbon reservoirs and the processes that move carbon between them.
I can model how photosynthesis and respiration move carbon.
I can predict how a change in one part of the carbon cycle affects the others.

Evaluate claims, evidence, and reasoning that the complex interactions in ecosystems maintain relatively consistent numbers and types of organisms in stable conditions, but changing conditions may result in a new ecosystem.
I can describe how interactions keep an ecosystem stable.
I can evaluate whether a claim is supported by evidence and reasoning.
I can explain how a disturbance can lead to a new ecosystem.

column3: HS-LS2-7: Human impact on the environment and biodiversity
column4: Design, evaluate, and refine a solution for reducing the impacts of human activities on the environment and biodiversity.
I can identify human activities that affect the environment and biodiversity.
I can design a solution using criteria and constraints.
I can evaluate and refine a solution using evidence.
Evaluate the evidence for the role of group behavior on individual and species' chances to survive and reproduce.
I can describe examples of group behavior.
I can use evidence to evaluate how group behavior affects survival and reproduction.

column3: HS-LS3-1: DNA and chromosomes code for traits
column4: Ask questions to clarify relationships about the role of DNA and chromosomes in coding the instructions for characteristic traits passed from parents to offspring.
I can explain the relationship between DNA, genes, and chromosomes.
I can ask questions that clarify how traits are passed from parents to offspring.
I can use Punnett squares to predict inheritance.

Make and defend a claim based on evidence that inheritable genetic variations may result from (1) new genetic combinations through meiosis, (2) viable errors occurring during replication, and/or (3) mutations caused by environmental factors.
I can explain how meiosis creates new genetic combinations.
I can describe how replication errors and mutations create variation.
I can make and defend a claim about the source of a variation using evidence.

column3: HS-LS3-3: Variation and distribution of traits
column4: Apply concepts of statistics and probability to explain the variation and distribution of expressed traits in a population.
I can calculate and interpret trait frequencies in a population.
I can use probability to explain the distribution of traits.
I can explain how the environment and genes together shape trait variation.
Communicate scientific information that common ancestry and biological evolution are supported by multiple lines of empirical evidence.
I can describe lines of evidence for evolution, such as fossils, anatomy, embryology, and DNA.
I can read a cladogram or phylogenetic tree.
I can communicate how multiple lines of evidence support common ancestry.

Construct an explanation based on evidence that the process of evolution primarily results from four factors: (1) the potential for a species to increase in number, (2) the heritable genetic variation of individuals in a species, (3) competition for limited resources, and (4) the proliferation of those organisms that are better able to survive and reproduce in the environment.
I can name and describe the four factors of natural selection.
I can use evidence to explain how the four factors lead to evolution in a population.
Apply concepts of statistics and probability to support explanations that organisms with an advantageous heritable trait tend to increase in proportion to organisms lacking this trait.
I can identify an advantageous heritable trait in a given environment.
I can analyze data showing changes in trait proportions over generations.
I can explain why advantageous traits become more common.
Construct an explanation based on evidence for how natural selection leads to adaptation of populations.
I can distinguish adaptation of a population from change in an individual.
I can explain how natural selection leads to adaptation using evidence.

Evaluate the evidence supporting claims that changes in environmental conditions may result in (1) increases in the number of individuals of some species, (2) the emergence of new species over time, and (3) the extinction of other species.
I can explain how environmental change affects population sizes.
I can describe how isolation can lead to new species.
I can evaluate evidence for claims about extinction and speciation.

column3: HS-LS4-6: Reducing human impact on biodiversity
column4: Create or revise a simulation to test a solution to mitigate adverse impacts of human activity on biodiversity.
I can create or revise a simulation of a human impact on biodiversity.
I can use simulation results to evaluate a proposed solution.
